For children due to start Reception
A very warm welcome to Braishfield Primary School! We are delighted to introduce you to our vibrant and nurturing school community. At Braishfield, we provide a positive, supportive environment where children are encouraged to grow into happy, kind, honest, and respectful individuals.
Though we are a small school of just over 100 pupils, our aspirations are anything but small. We are deeply committed to inspiring every child, engaging them in meaningful learning experiences, and discovering and nurturing their unique talents.
Starting school is a significant milestone for both children and their families—an exciting chapter that can also bring a few natural nerves. Our goal is to make this transition as smooth and joyful as possible, giving every child the very best start to their primary education journey.
We welcome visits from prospective families and offer school tours for parents and carers of children due to start school. If you're planning ahead for a September start, we’d be delighted to hear from you. Please contact Mrs. Ewens in the school office at 01794 368359 or email adminoffice@braishfield.hants.sch.uk. Our official tour dates take place in the Autumn term, but we welcome you to visit at any time throughout the year.
We look forward to meeting you.

pageCache.text:
Meet the Governors
Welcome to the Governors Information Page
In September 2025 there were no Governors that declared a Pecuniary Interest, Governors will be asked at every meeting if this has changed.
I am passionate about education and committed to contributing positively to the development of a local school community. Having been actively involved in my sons education, I understand the pivotal role that education plays in shaping the future of individuals and enabling every child to achieve their potential. As a school governor, I aim to bring my skills gained from my career in IT Program Management, such as strategic planning, communication, budget management to help the school achieve its required objectives. I believe in an inclusive and supportive learning environment that supports the needs of every student while collaborating with fellow governors, teachers, and parents to ensure the school's policies align with the best interests of the students.
Vice Chair of Governors
I have been on the board of governors for two years and have enjoyed the opportunity working with a team of governors and staff that want the best for Braishfield Primary School. I have two children that attend Braishfield Primary School and one that completed her primary education at Braishfield Primary School, so I have been a part of the culture for many years. I work in the building and construction project management so bring the project management and little building expertise to the governing board; this is out worked as the H&S governor for the school.
Since 2013, I’ve had the privilege of serving as a Governor at Braishfield, stepping in and out of the role over the years. Today, as a co-opted Governor and Co-chair, I’m proud to help guide the school’s future. Braishfield holds a special place in my heart—not only as an institution but as a community. Both my children attended the school, and I’ve loved watching them grow up in the village alongside my husband, family, and an assortment of pets. With my past experience as a Governor, I’m eager to contribute to the school’s development, ensuring every child thrives and receives the best possible education.
This is my first time within a governing body, joining as a parent governor due to my little girl attending Braishfield Primary School. I have lived in Romsey my whole life and I am looking forward to working with the other governors and the school to support in the teaching and learning environment for all the children in attendance.
I have experience in training and development, people management along with some Human Resource elements which I look forward to utilising to compliment the governing body’s already talented skillset.
My son currently attends Braishfield primary school and hopefully my daughter will join him in a couple of years. I feel it is important to support the school in anyway and to maintain the high standards it currently offers.
I have experience in decision making, risk management, budget management, people management and HR issues. I work with communities, key stakeholders and partners daily.
This is the second time of being a governor at Braishfield. My first term, as a parent governor, was whilst my two sons were pupils at the school. I have rejoined the governing body because the school and education are very special to me. I started my career as a primary school teacher, before I left the sector to focus on other things. During the time that my boys were at Braishfield, my passion for helping children achieve the best that they could was re-ignited and was the reason for becoming a governor and the reason for returning. My career as a product manager provides me with lots of experience developing vision and strategy to deliver impact and value.
I am proud to serve as a governor at our school and to contribute to a community that places children at the heart of everything it does. I am committed to ensuring that all pupils’ educational needs are recognised and met and believe strongly in creating opportunities for every child to achieve their best, whatever their starting point. As a governor, I work with the leadership team to help maintain high expectations, promote inclusive practice, and ensure that resources and decisions always support positive outcomes for children.
By drawing on my professional experience in programme management and my commitment to education, I aim to play an active role in helping the school continue to grow, improve, and provide the very best for the children and families it serves.

Pupil Premium Funding
The Pupil Premium Funding is additional funding allocated to schools to help address inequalities in rates of progress and attainment of vulnerable groups.
It is aimed at closing the attainment gap between pupils from vulnerable families and their peers. It is allocated to schools to work with pupils who have been registered for free school meals at any point in the last six years (known as Ever 6 FSM). Schools also receive funding for pupils from families who are in the armed services or pupils who have been looked after continuously for more than 6 months.
Headteachers and school leaders decide how to use the Pupil Premium funding to meet the particular needs of their pupils and are held accountable for the difference it makes.
To learn how Braishfield Primary School is currently using the Pupil Premium funding please follow the link to this year's Strategy Statement.
At Braishfield Primary School, we aim to ensure that all children are successful and that any barriers to learning are removed. We are focused on 'closing the gap' in rates of progress and attainment between those children who are receiving Pupil Premium and those who are not.
We invest the Pupil Premium funding received by the school in providing 'additional learning' in small groups, one-to-one booster sessions or through releasing the class teacher to give Pupil Premium children extra teaching. We provide emotional and pastoral support through our trained ELSA (Emotional Literacy Support Assistant) and enrichment activities such as music lessons and school trips.
We use rigorous tracking to analyse the progress of our Pupil Premium children, identifying focus areas, deciding how they will be addressed and assessing their impact. Teachers understand their accountability for the progress of all children and their achievement is a standard item on the agenda for every full Governing Body meeting. We also have a specific Governor who monitors progress of Pupil Premium children and challenges school leaders by holding them to account.
